title: A red apple under a green lamp
hook: In a dark room, light a ripe red apple with a pure green lamp. What colour do you see?

knows: apples are red and leaves are green
light comes in colours, as in a rainbow
doesNotKnow: that objects send back some colours of light and absorb the rest
that white light is a mix of colours

misconception: A red apple has its own redness that it shows under any light.
objective: The learner can explain that an object's colour is the part of the light falling on it that it sends back, so a red apple under pure green light has almost nothing to return and looks nearly black.

claims.text: An object's colour comes from the light it sends back (reflects); the colours it does not send back are absorbed.
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e, section 26.3 Color and Color Vision: the colour of an object is set by the wavelengths it reflects; the rest are absorbed.

claims.text: White light is a mix of colours; on the stage it is drawn as equal red, green and blue.
claims.source: Newton's prism experiments; OpenStax College Physics 2e, section 25.5 Dispersion. The equal three-band split is a drawing simplification (real white light is a continuous spectrum), labelled 'toy values' on stage.

claims.text: A red apple reflects red light strongly and absorbs most green and blue light.
claims.source: Apple skin reflectance spectra (e.g. Merzlyak, Solovchenko and Gitelson 2003, 'Reflectance spectral features and non-destructive estimation of chlorophyll, carotenoid and anthocyanin content in apple fruit', Postharvest Biology and Technology 27:197-211): red (anthocyanin-rich) skin reflects weakly at 500-600 nm and strongly above about 640 nm. Verifier must confirm against a real curve before publication.

claims.text: The stage's reflectance values (apple 80% red, 5% green, 5% blue; banana 80%, 70%, 10%; leaf 8%, 45%, 6%) are illustrative toy values, not measurements.
claims.source: Chosen by the builder to match the qualitative shape of each object's reflectance (red / yellow / green). Labelled 'toy values' on the stage. REFL table in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: With these values the apple sends back 30% of white light, 80% of red, 5% of green and 5% of blue.
claims.source: Fraction returned = sum over bands of reflectance x lamp band / lamp bands lit: white (0.80 + 0.05 + 0.05) / 3 = 0.30; red 0.80; green 0.05; blue 0.05. Computed by back() in Demo.tsx; node check in build note.

claims.text: Under pure green light a red apple returns only a little green, so it looks very dark green, almost black.
claims.source: Follows from c1 and c3: a monochromatic green lamp contains no red light to reflect; the small green reflectance returns a dim green. Pure single-colour lamp and no other light in the room are stated on the stage ('Dark room, one lamp').

claims.text: A yellow banana sends back both red and green light, so under a red lamp it looks red and under a green lamp it looks green.
claims.source: Yellow surfaces reflect long and middle wavelengths (OpenStax College Physics 2e, 26.3). With the toy values: red lamp 80%, green lamp 70% returned.

recall.question: A white shirt is lit only by a pure red lamp in a dark room. It looks...
recall.why: A white shirt sends back every colour that falls on it, but the only colour arriving is red, so red is all it can return.
